## Referrer and URL behavior

By default, `referrer` is `document.referrer` from the browser, and `url` is the canonical URL on the page. On SPA navigation (no full page reload), there is **no new referrer** — it remains the original first-page value. To override this, manually set `referrer` and `url` in the context object.

### Page call with custom referrer/url:
```js
analytics.page({
  referrer: 'https://segment.com/',
  url: 'https://segment.com/pricing/?ref=nav'
})
```

### Track call with custom referrer/url:
```js
analytics.track('Example Event', {}, {page: {
  referrer: 'https://segment.com/',
  url: 'https://segment.com/pricing/?ref=nav'
}})
```

## Tracking emulated page views

SPAs must manually update the URL in the address bar to emulate traditional page navigation. Since resources load on initial page load, the standard Analytics.js Page call won't fire again on SPA navigation.

**Setup:**
- Place the Analytics.js snippet in `<head>` but remove the auto Page call.
- Call `analytics.page()` manually whenever you emulate a page load — from the same routing/view-update logic:

```js
// The new view has been called to render
analytics.page("Home")
```

Pass additional properties as the second argument to `analytics.page()`. Segment recommends using variables for page properties and automating the Page call to your SPA framework's routing service.

## analytics.ready() function

`analytics.ready()` lets you call native integrations that Segment loads before they initialize (e.g., load a live chat widget only for unidentified users).

**Caveat:** Code in the `<head>` snippet executes only on initial load/refresh. `analytics.ready()` won't run on each SPA navigation — native tool calls won't re-execute on emulated page views.

## UTM tracking

Segment automatically captures UTMs in URLs. You can also manually pass UTMs into context campaign fields (see Segment docs for campaign field structure).
